relevance_note: The paper describes two patients with ABCA1 variants: "We describe two patients with Tangier disease (TD)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (two first-hand case descriptions plus a narrative review); rows were written by a short script in the scratch directory whose values were all typed from my reading, then every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Table 1 has patients as columns (column headers 'Patient 1', 'Patient 2'). Labels: 'Patient 1' is the paper's most frequent form; 'Patient 2' and 'Patient # 2' each occur twice, and 'Patient 2' was chosen to match Table 1 and 'Patient 1'. In scope: Patient 1, Patient 2, and Patient 1's mother and brother (tested heterozygous carriers of c.1759 C > T). Out of scope: Patient 2's parents (not tested, unaffected: 'Neither parent demonstrated clinical or biochemical features suggestive of TD'); the 'at least one additional individual with TD' from the testing laboratory's internal data carrying c.1733 C > G (indefinite, no identifiable person); Fredrickson's 'two children from Tangier Island' [2] (group-level description only, no individual-level fact). Age at diagnosis taken from Table 1 row 'Age at diagnosis (year)' (5 and 11); the text says Patient 2 was referred at about 14 'following a recent genetic diagnosis of TD' after low HDL-C at about 11, so his genetic diagnosis may have been later than 11. Table 1 lipid values: triglycerides (84 vs acceptable < 75; 102 vs acceptable < 90) and LDL-C (68 and 62, normal range 50–110) are printed with reference ranges but not interpreted by the authors, so 'hypertriglyceridemia' and 'low LDL cholesterol' are left not reported. Normal whole examinations/investigations (D-27) were recorded as written and exclude nothing more specific: Patient 1 'Neurological examination was normal' (neuropathy items left not reported); Patient 2 normal laboratory investigations including complete blood count (thrombocytopenia not excluded), normal abdominal ultrasonography (splenomegaly/hepatomegaly not excluded), normal ophthalmologic and neurologic evaluations (corneal opacity/neuropathy not excluded), normal CCTA and exercise stress test (coronary artery disease left not reported), unremarkable upper endoscopy and biopsy (intestinal lipid deposits not excluded). Patient 2 denied enlarged tonsils but orange tonsil colour is not addressed, so 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' is not reported; his denial of recurrent throat infections and tonsillectomy excludes 'recurrent tonsillitis or tonsillectomy'. The MASS phenotype for Patient 2 was 'considered' and judged incidental by the authors; recorded only via its component findings (mitral valve, arachnodactyly, dolichostenomelia), not as a feature. Patient 1 c.1733 C > G: testing laboratory classified VUS, authors argue likely pathogenic; inheritance of this variant left not reported (only in trans is stated; the father was not described as tested). Patient 1 c.1759 C > T recorded inherited maternal because the mother is stated heterozygous for it. Functional evidence for c.1759 C > T taken from the sentence naming R587W among functionally characterized ECD1 variants (ref [4]); not copied to the relatives' rows. Relatives' sex taken from 'mother' and 'brother'. No contradictions found in the paper.
